final_candidates.decision_summary: Highest LOF proxy (z=0.973) with near-zero evolutionary tolerance; alanine substitution at a conserved catalytic-region arginine strongly predicted to abolish activity.
Strong LOF proxy (z=0.826) and zero mutant frequency in homologs; bulky charged residue at a conserved glycine likely disrupts backbone packing and function.
Well-characterized thermolabile MTHFR variant with pathogenic-class phenotype and zero MSA frequency for valine, supporting reduced enzyme activity.

stop_reason.detail: Evidence already resolves the Top-3 ordering and remaining tools cannot meaningfully change it.

history.rationale: Arginine residues in the catalytic domain frequently coordinate the negatively charged folate/FAD cofactor; substitution disrupts binding and turnover. Known MTHFR pathogenic variants cluster around conserved catalytic arginines.
Highest AlphaMissense LOF proxy (0.973) and low mutant frequency among homologs support strong disruption at a conserved arginine likely involved in substrate/regulatory binding.
Highest phenotype LOF proxy (z=0.973) and low evolutionary tolerance; remains strongest LOF candidate.

Glycines in tight turns of the TIM barrel are structurally essential; introducing a bulky charged arginine should sterically disrupt the fold and abolish activity. Backbone-flexibility Gly positions are highly mutation-sensitive.
Pathogenic prediction (0.826) with zero homolog tolerance for Arg at a buried Gly; charge/bulk introduction at a glycine is a classic destabilizing LOF substitution.
Strong phenotype score (z=0.826) with zero mutant frequency in MSA; charged bulky substitution at conserved glycine likely disruptive.
Prolines constrain backbone geometry; loss at a conserved position can distort the domain and reduce activity. Moderate-confidence structural disruption candidate.
Pathogenic (0.800) but weaker, and evolution evidence has reduced applicability (coverage 13/23); Pro->Ala is a milder chemical change than the top two.
Good phenotype score (z=0.800) but MSA applicability was low (0.56); ranked just below A222V which now has stronger combined support.

This corresponds to the well-known thermolabile MTHFR polymorphism region; introducing a bulkier residue destabilizes the enzyme and reduces activity. Empirically associated with reduced MTHFR function.
A222V is the known thermolabile catalytic-domain variant with partial LOF; retain and evaluate with phenotype/PLM next round.
Pathogenic-class phenotype (0.632) plus zero MSA frequency for V supports LOF; this is the well-known thermolabile A222V variant, promoted above P348A.
Acidic residue adjacent to a functionally sensitive region; charge removal may perturb catalytic geometry. Reasonable LOF candidate pending evidence.
Untested by tools this round; keep active pending phenotype evaluation of a potential catalytic-domain acidic residue.
Lowest phenotype score (z=0.442, ambiguous class) and A is tolerated in ~9% of homologs, indicating weak LOF likelihood.
